claims.text: The initial material is single-phase fcc FeCoNi or an FeCoNi-based high-entropy-alloy derivative.
The initial material has coercivity no greater than 100 Oe.
The initial material has high saturation magnetization.
Uniaxial stress-assisted annealing can induce a slight tetragonal distortion in the nominally fcc lattice.
The stress-induced tetragonal distortion will enhance magnetocrystalline anisotropy.
The tetragonal distortion will create effective domain-wall pinning sites.
Enhanced magnetocrystalline anisotropy and domain-wall pinning will increase coercivity.
Stress-assisted annealing will raise coercivity above 100 Oe relative to an identically annealed unstressed control.
The coercive field could reach several hundred Oe.
Stress-assisted annealing will preserve high saturation magnetization.
High saturation magnetization is inherent to the fcc phase in the proposed material.
The treatment must retain a single phase and avoid secondary phases or significant compositional segregation.
Excessive lattice distortion might compromise saturation magnetization.
The magnitude of the coercivity increase will depend on applied stress and annealing parameters.
Replacing Co with Cr in AlCoFeNi substantially reduces saturation magnetization and increases coercivity.
Composition and annealing temperature can affect B2 plus BCC decomposition in Al-Co-Cr-Fe-Ni alloys.

contradictions.description: The mediator is a tetragonal distortion, which lowers cubic fcc symmetry, while the boundary requires retention of a single-phase fcc structure. The hypothesis does not define whether 'fcc' includes a coherently strained face-centered tetragonal state or specify an allowable distortion threshold.
